newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 97/98 capital spending seen up 3.2 pct--MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan 97/98 capital spending seen up 3.2 pct--MITI.

text.p: Japanese firms plan a 3.2 percent rise in capital spending in fiscal 1997/98 from a year earlier, an increase for the third year in a row, according to a Trade Ministry survey released on Thursday.
Manufacturers plan to raise capital expenditures by 3.8 percent from the previous business year, while non-manufacturers plan an increase of 2.9 percent, the survey said.
Capital spending for fiscal 1996/97 ended on March 31 was expected to have risen 5.8 percent from a year earlier, it said.
Among manufacturers, the car and general machinery sectors were the most upbeat, planning year-on-year rises in capital investment of 19.4 percent and 18.9 percent, respectively.
In contrast, large declines were planned of 19.9 percent for the steel sector and 17.3 percent for the oil refining sector.
Among non-manufacturers, leasing-related business was particularly healthy, the survey said.
The Trade Ministry conducted the survey in late March, receiving replies from 1,338 firms with a capital base of over 100 million yen.
